key_finding: Reviewer's Tier 2 levers FAILED in our testing. Higher N → earlier dt-collapse (opposite of reviewer's hypothesis). Higher min_particles → marginal improvement only at low N. Longer t_end → shorter achieved t_max (more sim time = more densification). T215p config (N=3k, min=64, t_end=0.07 = 70 Myr) is the PROVEN optimum within our parameter search.
explanation: Higher particle counts force the adaptive grid to subdivide bins more aggressively to maintain min_particles=64 minimum. Each subdivision creates a bin with fewer particles (eventually fewer than 64), prompting more subdivisions. With min_particles=32, this happens much faster (509 splits at N=10k). With higher N + low min_particles, the core bins quickly subdivide until individual bins have few particles, dt collapses, run dies.
reviewer_hypothesis_status: Reviewer's specific Tier 2 lever ('raise min_particles to 128') only works at low N (T215p baseline). At higher N, raising min_particles does NOT help because bins still split 100+ times. The fundamental limit is KiSS-SIDM v0.0.1's adaptive grid behavior, not particle count.
what_would_work: Tier 3 levers (NOT tested in this pilot, deferred to follow-up): (i) subcycled time integration in inner core, (ii) freeze refinement after density threshold, (iii) cap minimum bin size in core (not global min_particles), (iv) restart from last good snapshot with coarsening. These require KiSS-SIDM code modifications, not just parameter changes.
conclusion: Tier 1+2 future work did NOT extend T215 reach beyond 70 Myr. §10.5b conclusion (t_core not reached, methods-only contribution) stands. Tier 3 code modifications required for actual t_core measurement.
